authors: Stanstrup J, Neumann S, Vrhovšek U
title: PredRet: Prediction of Retention Time by Direct Mapping between Multiple Chromatographic Systems
verification: Crossref /works record (title match) and PubMed PMID 26289378 abstract retrieved this session; methods read from the open-access PDF (openpub.fmach.it).
category: Calibrant/overlap-based projection between chromatographic systems
problem: Share experimental RTs across labs and chromatographic systems (CSs) so that RT can help discriminate isomers in untargeted LC-MS.
data: Community-uploaded experimental RT database (predret.org) of several RP and HILIC CSs, with up to about 400 predicted RTs per CS at publication.
method: Pairwise robust, monotonically constrained GAMs (mgcv, sigmoid-weighted penalized constrained least squares) fitted on compounds measured on both CSs, with at least 10 shared compounds required.
uncertainty_method: Bootstrap (1000 resamples) 99% prediction intervals; predictions whose PI is wider than 2 min or 20% of RT are discarded, and the authors call the PIs anticonservative.
transfer_setting: Experimental-to-experimental projection between pairs of CSs of the same chromatography type; the query compound must already have a measured RT in a source CS.
main_results: Median prediction error 0.01-0.28 min and median PI width 0.08-1.86 min across CSs.
code_available: Yes: R package for querying the database (github.com/stanstrup/PredRet) and web service predret.org, as stated in the paper.
limitations: Cannot predict compounds never measured on an overlapping system, and its PIs have no coverage guarantee; the authors advise against using them as strict exclusion filters.
relevance_to_study: Canonical monotone calibrant-mapping baseline and the archetype of heuristic (bootstrap) RT intervals that our jackknife+ conformal windows are meant to replace with guaranteed coverage.

authors: Abate-Pella D, Freund DM, Ma Y, Simón-Manso Y, Hollender J, Broeckling CD, Huhman DV, Krokhin OV, Stoll DR, Hegeman AD, Kind T, Fiehn O, Schymanski EL, Prenni JE, Sumner LW, Boswell PG
title: Retention projection enables accurate calculation of liquid chromatographic retention times across labs and methods
verification: PubMed PMID 26292625 (title match) and author-manuscript full text PMC4556278 retrieved this session.
category: Physics-based cross-lab RT transfer using calibration standards
problem: Calculate gradient RTs across laboratories and methods more reliably than linear retention indices (LRIs).
data: Eight-lab study with one test mixture (20 instrument-calibration standards plus 19 test compounds) on Eclipse Plus C18 columns, using isocratic k-vs-phi data from a reference lab.
method: Retention projection from isocratic k-vs-phi relationships, combined with back-calculation of each lab's effective gradient and dead-time profiles from the co-injected calibration standards.
uncertainty_method: None beyond reported error ranges (for example ±0.27 to ±0.99 s for method 1); no prediction intervals.
transfer_setting: Same stationary and mobile phase, transferred across instruments, gradients and flow rates using calibration standards run on the target system.
main_results: For uncharged compounds, projections were on average 22-fold more accurate than LRIs under lab-chosen gradients and 2-fold more accurate under nominally identical conditions.
code_available: Yes: open-source Java software (retentionprediction.org/hplc/development) and an open k-vs-phi database.
limitations: Every compound needs measured isocratic k-vs-phi relationships on the same column chemistry, which the authors call a major drawback; charged compounds were less accurate because of column ageing.
relevance_to_study: Mechanistic calibrant-based transfer baseline showing that calibrant runs can absorb instrument-level differences, but it cannot cover novel structures as an ML base score can.

authors: Bach E, Szedmak S, Brouard C, Böcker S, Rousu J
title: Liquid-chromatography retention order prediction for metabolite identification
verification: PubMed PMID 30423079 record and abstract retrieved by DOI this session (title match).
category: Retention-order (pairwise ranking) learning across LC systems
problem: Use LC information for metabolite identification even though absolute RTs do not transfer between systems.
data: Heterogeneous public RT datasets from different LC systems and configurations, pooled without tedious pre-processing.
method: Ranking SVM learning a retention-order score from molecular representations, then combined with MS/MS scores over a whole LC-MS/MS run.
uncertainty_method: None (order scores only).
transfer_setting: Train on pooled multi-system data and predict elution order, not times, on other systems; chromatographic conditions are not encoded.
main_results: Showed that retention order is much better conserved between instruments than RT, and that combining order with MS/MS scores improves identification.
code_available: Yes: version.aalto.fi/gitlab/bache1/retention_order_prediction (stated in abstract).
limitations: Gives no absolute RTs or tolerance windows and cannot represent condition-specific changes in elution order.
relevance_to_study: Direct conceptual precursor of our pairwise-ranking retention-order base score; we add condition-aware multi-system training on RepoRT, calibrant mapping and calibrated windows.

authors: Bouwmeester R, Martens L, Degroeve S
title: Comprehensive and Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Small Molecule LC Retention Time Prediction
verification: Crossref record (title match; bioRxiv preprint relation) and PubMed PMID 30702864 abstract retrieved this session; repository README checked.
category: Single-system ML RT prediction benchmark
problem: Determine which ML algorithms and feature sets work best for small-molecule LC RT prediction.
data: 36 distinct metabolomics RT datasets (raw data from the Aicheler et al. set, MoNA and PredRet) with two feature sets.
method: Systematic comparison of seven machine-learning algorithms plus blending of model types.
uncertainty_method: None reported (point predictions).
transfer_setting: Setup-specific models trained and tested within each dataset; no cross-system transfer.
main_results: No single algorithm was best on all datasets, and blending models reduced errors on outliers.
code_available: Yes: github.com/RobbinBouwmeester/tRPredictionOverview (data, scripts, models).
limitations: Needs substantial training data from the target system and gives only point predictions.
relevance_to_study: Shows that base-model accuracy depends on the dataset, which motivates model-agnostic calibrated windows; it is also a source of benchmark datasets.

authors: Domingo-Almenara X, Guijas C, Billings E, Montenegro-Burke JR, Uritboonthai W, Aisporna AE, Chen E, Benton HP, Siuzdak G
title: The METLIN small molecule dataset for machine learning-based retention time prediction
verification: Crossref and PubMed PMID 31862874 records plus full text PMC6925099 retrieved this session.
category: Large single-system RT dataset with DL model and predicted-to-experimental projection
problem: RT prediction accuracy is limited by the small size of experimental datasets.
data: SMRT: 80,038 small molecules measured on one RP HPLC-MS method (Zorbax Extend-C18), with projection tests on PredRet CMs using HMDB/KEGG candidates.
method: Fingerprint-based deep-learning regressor; predicted RTs were projected to other CMs by a fourth-order polynomial fitted on 50 randomly selected known molecules.
uncertainty_method: None; candidate-filter RT thresholds were chosen post hoc from ROC curves (relative error 10-27.5%).
transfer_setting: Predicted-to-experimental projection to four external PredRet CMs (FEM_long, LIFE_old, RIKEN, FEM_orbitrap_plasma).
main_results: Median relative and absolute errors were 4.6% and 35 s, with the correct identity in the top 3 in up to 70% of cases, yet ROC-tuned thresholds discarded 21-41% of correct identities.
code_available: Yes: data and R scripts on Figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.8038913).
limitations: The authors concluded that predicted-experimental RT filtering is not robust, because the threshold varied strongly with the random projection subset; elution order is not conserved across HILIC methods.
relevance_to_study: Main pretraining resource, and the clearest documentation that heuristic ROC-tuned windows lose many true identities, which is our core motivation.

authors: Bonini P, Kind T, Tsugawa H, Barupal DK, Fiehn O
title: Retip: Retention Time Prediction for Compound Annotation in Untargeted Metabolomics
verification: Crossref and PubMed PMID 32390414 records plus full text PMC8715951 retrieved this session.
category: Single-system ML RT tool integrated into annotation software
problem: Raise confidence in untargeted LC-MS/MS annotations by predicting RT from structure.
data: Fiehn HILIC set (about 970-981 metabolites, BEH Amide) and RIKEN PlaSMA RPLC set (852 specialized metabolites).
method: R package with random forest, BRNN, XGBoost, LightGBM and Keras on CDK descriptors, with export of predictions to MS-DIAL and MS-FINDER.
uncertainty_method: Fixed ±1 min RT windows (about the MAE) for candidate exclusion; no interval model.
transfer_setting: None; users retrain on their own chromatographic method.
main_results: Keras MAE was 0.78 min (HILIC) and 0.57 min (RPLC), and ±1 min filtering excluded 68% of candidate structures in plasma HILIC data.
code_available: Yes: R package (retip.app, GitHub).
limitations: ±1 min windows held only 87% (RP) and 65% (HILIC) of test true positives and excluded about 25% of true positives overall, with no per-compound adaptation.
relevance_to_study: Representative fixed-minute window heuristic that our conformal windows are benchmarked against on coverage versus decoy elimination, for both RP and HILIC.

authors: Bouwmeester R, Martens L, Degroeve S
title: Generalized Calibration Across Liquid Chromatography Setups for Generic Prediction of Small-Molecule Retention Times
verification: PubMed PMID 32281370 abstract and Crossref record of the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2020.01.14.905844) retrieved this session; layer details from the bioRxiv full text via WebFetch.
category: Calibration of predicted RTs across LC setups
problem: Avoid fitting a new RT model for each setup by mapping models between experimental setups.
data: Many public RT datasets (setups); preprint learning curves use 20-100 calibration analytes from the target setup.
method: Three layers: setup-specific regressors, GAM (mgcv) calibration of each model's predictions to target RTs, and an elastic-net combination of the calibrated predictions.
uncertainty_method: None for individual predictions (the preprint shows only an SD band for the GAM fit).
transfer_setting: Transfer of models trained on other setups to a target setup using a modest set of calibration analytes.
main_results: Generalized calibration gave substantially higher elution-peak prediction accuracy than setup-specific models.
code_available: Yes: github.com/compomics/CALLC.
limitations: Point predictions only; accuracy depends on the number and coverage of calibrants, and tolerances are not coverage-controlled.
relevance_to_study: Closest ML precursor of our 'project a public model, then map with calibrants' stage, but it provides no calibrated windows.

authors: Yang Q, Ji H, Lu H, Zhang Z
title: Prediction of Liquid Chromatographic Retention Time with Graph Neural Networks to Assist in Small Molecule Identification
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 33406817 abstract retrieved this session; GitHub README checked.
category: Single-system GNN RT prediction with transfer learning
problem: Improve RT prediction accuracy for structure identification without hand-crafted descriptors.
data: METLIN SMRT (RP) for training, with transfer to other datasets of the same chromatography type.
method: End-to-end graph neural network on molecular graphs, compared with RF, Bayesian ridge, CNN and DLM baselines, plus fine-tuning for transfer.
uncertainty_method: None.
transfer_setting: Pretrain on SMRT, then fine-tune on target datasets of the same chromatography type (requires target training data).
main_results: Mean and median relative errors of 4.9% and 3.2% on SMRT, the best among the compared models.
code_available: Yes: github.com/Qiong-Yang/GNN-RT (preprocess, train and transfer-learning scripts).
limitations: Transfer needs fine-tuning data from each target system, and it offers neither uncertainty nor a calibrant-only protocol.
relevance_to_study: Representative pretrain/fine-tune paradigm that cannot operate with only n≈10-50 calibrants.

authors: Aalizadeh R, Alygizakis NA, Schymanski EL, Krauss M, Schulze T, Ibáñez M, McEachran AD, Chao A, Williams AJ, Gago-Ferrero P, Covaci A, Moschet C, Young TM, Hollender J, Slobodnik J, Thomaidis NS
title: Development and Application of Liquid Chromatographic Retention Time Indices in HRMS-Based Suspect and Nontarget Screening
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 34382770 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
category: Calibrant-based RT index harmonisation for NTS
problem: Make LC RTs comparable between laboratories as supporting evidence in HRMS suspect and nontarget screening.
data: Two sets of 18 calibrants (ESI+ and ESI−) chosen from 2,123 compounds, with external validation on other instruments and LC conditions coordinated by NORMAN.
method: Unified retention time index (RTI, 1-1000) calibrated on the calibrant elution pattern, plus QSRR models that predict RTI.
uncertainty_method: QSRR applicability domains flag substances whose predictions should be treated with caution; no calibrated intervals.
transfer_setting: Cross-lab transfer of RP RTs through the calibrant-based RTI.
main_results: The RTI system was validated externally and used to remove false-positive annotations in two NTS examples (online at rti.chem.uoa.gr).
code_available: Web tool rti.chem.uoa.gr; source code not stated in the abstract.
limitations: Applicability-domain flags are qualitative; a later study (Malm & Kruve 2025) found RTIs sensitive to nonlinear gradient programs.
relevance_to_study: NTS standard for calibrant-based harmonisation; our calibrant mapping with conformal windows adds quantitative, coverage-controlled tolerances in the same workflow.

authors: García CA, Gil-de-la-Fuente A, Barbas C, Otero A
title: Probabilistic metabolite annotation using retention time prediction and meta-learned projections
verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 35672784 and full text PMC9172150 retrieved this session.
category: Few-calibrant probabilistic projection with meta-learning across chromatographic methods
problem: Project SMRT-trained RT predictions to a lab's chromatographic method from very few identified molecules while quantifying uncertainty.
data: SMRT (80,038 RTs) for base models; PredRet CMs as meta-tasks, with FEM long, FEM orbitrap plasma, LIFE old and RIKEN as targets.
method: Regularized DNN base predictor plus a Gaussian-process projection whose prior (mean and kernel) is meta-learned on other CMs by minimizing a leave-one-out predictive loss.
uncertainty_method: GP posterior predictive 95% intervals, scored with the interval score; z-scores rank candidates.
transfer_setting: Leave-one-CM-out with 10-50 stratified calibrants from the target CM.
main_results: On SMRT the DNN reached MAE 39.2 s and MedAE 17.2 s; the meta-learned GP had the best scaled interval score in 3 of 4 CMs, and the correct molecule was in the top 3 in 68% (10 calibrants) to 70% (50 calibrants) of queries.
code_available: Yes: github.com/constantino-garcia/cmmrt.
limitations: Gaussian, model-based intervals without finite-sample coverage guarantees, tested on only four target CMs; the 1-D GP variance depends on the base predicted RT, not on molecule-level novelty.
relevance_to_study: Closest prior idea to our meta-learning across systems for few-calibrant intervals; we differ through jackknife+ conformal guarantees, molecule- and system-level difficulty normalisation, and evaluation on about 240 systems.

authors: Kretschmer F, Harrieder E-M, Hoffmann MA, Böcker S, Witting M
title: RepoRT: a comprehensive repository for small molecule retention times
verification: Crossref record (title match; preprint relation) and PubMed PMID 38191934 retrieved; content statistics from the Crossref record of ChemRxiv preprint v2 (10.26434/chemrxiv-2023-1mq73-v2); GitHub README checked.
category: Multi-system RT repository and benchmark
problem: No curated, machine-learning-ready RT data with chromatographic metadata existed for transferable prediction.
data: Preprint v2: 373 datasets, 8,809 unique compounds, 88,325 RT entries on 49 columns, with column, eluent and gradient metadata and column selectivity (HSM/Tanaka) parameters.
method: Curated GitHub-hosted repository with structure standardization, automated validation and a normalized column database.
uncertainty_method: Not applicable (data resource).
transfer_setting: Supports training and evaluation across many RP and HILIC systems with their metadata.
main_results: First comprehensive multi-system RT repository; it now underpins transferable models such as 2-step.
code_available: Yes: github.com/michaelwitting/RepoRT; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16267767.
limitations: Datasets differ widely in size and metadata completeness.
relevance_to_study: Our training and evaluation source (about 240 RP systems with leave-source-out folds, plus HILIC tests).

authors: Zhang Y, Liu F, Li XQ, Gao Y, Li KC, Zhang QH
title: Generic and accurate prediction of retention times in liquid chromatography by post-projection calibration
verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 38459241 and full text PMC10923921 retrieved this session.
category: Calibrant-based projection with external reference calibration
problem: Give generic RT predictions across chromatographic methods (CMs) to support candidate annotation.
data: MCMRT: 343 molecules on 30 RP CMs; QSRR trained on 1,820 emerging contaminants (CM 03p); 2,935 candidates for 112 identities.
method: GP-regression projections (rational-quadratic kernel) fitted on 35 calibrants, plus a re-projection from a similar laboratory CM (ReICM) that calibrates the projected RTs.
uncertainty_method: No interval model; candidates were filtered with a heuristic threshold of twice the RMSE for each output CM.
transfer_setting: Public CM to local CM, with 35 external calibrants measured on both.
main_results: Median projection error stayed below 3.2% of elution time, yet after calibration 6-20% of true identities were still filtered out and 29-43% of false candidates accepted.
code_available: Yes: MATLAB code and data at github.com/Yanzi-Zhang-oss/Post-projection-calibration-of-retention-time-across-liquid-chromatography-setups.
limitations: Needs a second, similar reference CM and 35 calibrants, and the ±2·RMSE windows have uncontrolled coverage.
relevance_to_study: Direct heuristic-window baseline (±k·RMSE) and calibrant-protocol comparator for our conformal windows and decoy-elimination evaluation.

authors: Xue J, Wang B, Ji H, Li W
title: RT-Transformer: retention time prediction for metabolite annotation to assist in metabolite identification
verification: Crossref record, PubMed PMID 38402516 and full text PMC10914443 retrieved this session.
category: Pretrain/fine-tune RT prediction
problem: Scalable RT prediction for any chromatographic method to support metabolite annotation.
data: SMRT (80,038) for pretraining; fine-tuning on 41 PredRet datasets (more than 80 compounds each) and five other CMs.
method: Graph attention network plus 1D-Transformer; the feature extractor is frozen and the output block fine-tuned on target data.
uncertainty_method: None; the filtering threshold was chosen from ROC curves (relative error 4.3-5.7%).
transfer_setting: Transfer learning to target CMs that have tens to hundreds of training compounds.
main_results: SMRT MAE 27.30 s (retained molecules) or 33.41 s (all); the ROC thresholds removed 80.9-85.4% of false identities, and the mean isomer filter rate was 59.35%.
code_available: Yes: github.com/01dadada/RT-Transformer and a Hugging Face web server (stated in paper).
limitations: Needs target fine-tuning data and uses global ROC-tuned thresholds without coverage control; a later study (2-step) found large accuracy drops under structure-disjoint splits.
relevance_to_study: State-of-the-art pretrain/fine-tune comparator, and an example of the global-threshold practice that our method replaces.

authors: Matyushin DD, Burov IA, Sholokhova AYu
title: Uncertainty Quantification and Flagging of Unreliable Predictions in Predicting Mass Spectrometry-Related Properties of Small Molecules Using Machine Learning
verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 39684785 and full text PMC11641629 retrieved this session.
category: Uncertainty estimation and flagging of unreliable RT predictions
problem: Predictions of RT, RI and CCS usually come without any per-molecule uncertainty.
data: SMRT (RT above 500 s, one RP system), NIST 17 GC retention indices (polar and non-polar) and a CCS [M+H]+ compilation.
method: Features from ensemble spread, similarity to the nearest training molecule (Tanimoto, cosine, Euclidean, MCS) and k-means cluster membership, fed to logistic regression or AutoML.
uncertainty_method: Binary classifier that predicts whether a prediction falls among the worst 15%.
transfer_setting: None (cross-validation within a single system).
main_results: ROC-AUC 0.73-0.82 across tasks (0.733 for LC RT with AutoML); error distributions were closer to exponential, sometimes Cauchy-like, than normal.
code_available: Yes: github.com/mtshn/uncertaintychem.
limitations: Produces flags rather than intervals, with no coverage guarantee, on a single chromatographic system.
relevance_to_study: Supports our difficulty features (novelty and similarity, ensemble disagreement); the heavy-tailed errors it reports motivate distribution-free conformal windows.

authors: Malm L, Kruve A
title: Do experimental projection methods outcompete retention time prediction models in non-target screening? A case study on LC/HRMS interlaboratory comparison data
verification: Crossref record (title match) and full text PMC12268317 (PMID 40671565) retrieved this session.
category: NTS evaluation of calibrant projection versus ML prediction across interlaboratory systems
problem: Test whether calibrant-based projections beat ML RT predictions for NTS on real routine laboratory systems.
data: NORMAN interlaboratory comparison: 41 calibrants and 45 suspects measured on 37 chromatographic systems; the ML model was trained on Aalizadeh et al. RT data.
method: RTI conversion followed by GAM projection (mgcv, k=6) fitted on calibrants detected in both systems, compared with a Mordred-descriptor ML prediction model.
uncertainty_method: None beyond RMSE and 95th-percentile absolute deviations, with F-tests on RMSE.
transfer_setting: Source system to NTS system through the shared detected calibrants (a subset of the 41).
main_results: Projection RMSE was 78.1 RTI units (7.8% of the range) versus 149.0 for prediction; calibrant and suspect RMSEs correlated weakly (R² 0.30), and projections failed outside the calibrant range (9.8% of suspects).
code_available: Yes: data and code in the ESI.
limitations: Small chemical space (86 chemicals), mostly RP systems, and no interval methodology.
relevance_to_study: Shows that calibrant residuals poorly predict suspect errors and that mobile-phase pH and column chemistry drive transfer error, which motivates our meta-learned, system-aware difficulty normalisation.

authors: Li Y, Dong K, Yu D, Huang D, Liu X, Xu G, Lin X
title: Prediction of Retention Time by Combining Multiple Data Sets with Chromatographic Parameter Vectorization and Transfer Learning
verification: PubMed PMID 40747624 record and abstract retrieved by DOI this session (title match); Crossref component records also seen.
category: Multi-dataset, condition-aware pretraining with fine-tuning
problem: RT models are tied to one column and set of conditions, and data sparsity limits accuracy.
data: 14 RPLC and 14 HILIC datasets.
method: MDL-TL: joint training over several datasets, with column and conditions vectorized by word2vec and autoencoders and appended to compound representations, then fine-tuned to each target system.
uncertainty_method: None reported in abstract.
transfer_setting: Pretrained multi-dataset model fine-tuned on each target system.
main_results: Beat five deep-learning and four machine-learning approaches, including SMRT-based transfer, on MAE, MedAE, MRE and R² in most cases.
code_available: Not determined (not stated in abstract and not found in web searches).
limitations: Requires target fine-tuning data, and reports neither uncertainty nor a calibrant-only evaluation.
relevance_to_study: Concurrent evidence that encoding chromatographic parameters helps multi-system learning, as in our base score.

authors: Wiczling P
title: Bayesian multilevel modeling of retention data informed by structural similarity of analytes
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41177069 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
category: Bayesian hierarchical retention modelling with structural similarity
problem: Retention models usually treat analytes as conditionally independent given their descriptors and ignore structural similarity.
data: Public isocratic RP-HPLC dataset of 1,026 analytes.
method: Multilevel multi-output Gaussian process with matrix-normal between-analyte variability whose row covariance is a Tanimoto similarity matrix.
uncertainty_method: Full Bayesian posterior predictive uncertainty.
transfer_setting: Within one dataset across isocratic chromatographic parameters; no cross-lab or cross-system transfer.
main_results: Adding structural similarity improved predictive performance, especially when data for related analytes were available.
code_available: Not determined (paywalled; not found in web searches).
limitations: Single isocratic dataset; the abstract does not report whether intervals stay calibrated under cross-system shift.
relevance_to_study: Supports Tanimoto-based novelty as a driver of RT predictive uncertainty, a feature family in our difficulty model.

authors: Beck AG, Jones G, Singh A, Fine J, Shrestha R, Barrientos RC, Sherer EC, Williams KB, Regalado EL, Aggarwal P
title: Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Multiple Conditions as a Framework for Streamlined Retention Time Prediction to Accelerate Method Development
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41627175 abstract retrieved; ChemRxiv preprint (10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-z39t1) via Crossref; uncertainty implementation read from public repository code (train_scripts/480_uncert.py).
category: Condition-aware RT prediction with uncertainty
problem: Speed up LC method screening by predicting RTs across column chemistries and buffer pH.
data: MCaRT: 480 Enamine analytes under 8 conditions (C18, cyano, phenyl and Gold aQ columns, each with TFA or ammonium acetate buffer) on a 5-min gradient.
method: GIN graph network initialised from SMRT-trained weights, with explicit column and buffer descriptors appended.
uncertainty_method: Per the public code, a heteroscedastic head (learned log-variance) plus MC dropout (100 passes) splits aleatoric and epistemic variance; the abstract reports calibrated uncertainty.
transfer_setting: Across four column chemistries and two buffers within one lab; analytes seen on one column improve predictions on others.
main_results: Cross-validated R² 0.86 and MAE 15.5 s, improving to R² 0.95 and MAE 8.2 s when analytes were seen on one column chemistry.
code_available: Yes: github.com/MSDLLCpapers/MRL-MC-Retention (code, weights, MCaRT data).
limitations: Single lab, one short gradient and eight conditions; the uncertainty is Gaussian and model-based without finite-sample guarantees, and the work targets method development rather than annotation or NTS.
relevance_to_study: Closest recent uncertainty-aware multi-condition RT model; our conformal windows add distribution-free coverage under cross-lab calibrant transfer.

authors: Xiong Z, Wang X, Liu J, Cong S, Yang Q, Ji H
title: Unified Multitask Modeling for Retention Time Prediction Across Chromatographic Conditions
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41885002 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
category: Multitask multi-condition RT prediction
problem: Condition-specific RT models fragment knowledge and scale poorly.
data: 28 RPLC and HILIC datasets.
method: Uni-RT: a unified multitask framework that learns from heterogeneous datasets together, capturing shared retention patterns and condition-specific differences.
uncertainty_method: None reported in abstract.
transfer_setting: Joint learning over the conditions represented in training; the abstract does not describe zero-shot transfer to unseen systems.
main_results: Higher accuracy and robustness than pooled or condition-specific models, with simpler deployment.
code_available: Not determined (not stated in abstract and not found in web searches).
limitations: Appears to need training data for each condition and provides no calibrated intervals.
relevance_to_study: Concurrent multi-system learner; it contrasts with our setting, where the target system offers only n≈10-50 calibrants.

authors: Deng J, Chen J, Wang J, Li X, Liu S, Ge L, Ying G-G, Chen C-E
title: Retention time prediction of emerging contaminants via transfer learning with graph neural networks
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 41621299 abstract retrieved this session (title match).
category: Transfer learning for NTS of emerging contaminants
problem: Predict RTs of environmental contaminants for LC-MS non-targeted analysis when standards are scarce.
data: Source domain METLIN-SMRT; target domain of 1,051 environmental pollutants.
method: Phased comparison of 5 GNN architectures, pretraining optimizers, training strategies and TL optimizers; the best was GIN3, fine-tuned with L-BFGS.
uncertainty_method: Applicability-domain assessment; no prediction intervals.
transfer_setting: SMRT to a single target environmental dataset by fine-tuning.
main_results: R² 0.894 versus 0.816 for the best conventional ML method, with a smaller train-test decline (8% versus 11-19%).
code_available: Not determined (paywalled; not found in web searches).
limitations: Evaluated on one target dataset with a train/test split; calibrant-only (n≈10-50) regimes and calibrated windows were not reported.
relevance_to_study: Environmental-NTS transfer baseline whose target-data needs exceed the calibrant-only budgets we study.

authors: Fadil F, Schmidt T, Amesoeder C, Heckscher S, Schoen M, Gronwald W, Oefner PJ, Spang R, Dettmer K
title: FastRet: Fast and Simple Retention Time Prediction in Liquid Chromatography
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 42670875 and full text PMC13508770 retrieved this session.
category: Practical RT tool with model adjustment from few remeasured compounds
problem: Fast, simple RT prediction plus adaptation to changed chromatographic conditions in untargeted metabolomics.
data: In-house RP (458), RP-AXMM (436) and HILIC (388) sets, Retip HILIC (970), six modified RP conditions and 14 external datasets.
method: LASSO or boosted regression trees on descriptors, selective measuring (cluster medoids) to choose compounds, and an adjustment model g(x, RT_base) learned from remeasured compounds.
uncertainty_method: None (point predictions with cross-validated performance estimates).
transfer_setting: Adjustment to modified conditions from about 25 selected remeasured metabolites.
main_results: Adjustment with 25 metabolites reached R² 0.74-0.84 on unseen metabolites (mean gain 0.22 over from-scratch models) and outperformed published methods in low-data transfer.
code_available: Yes: CRAN package FastRet, github.com/spang-lab/FastRet and the web app fastret.spang-lab.de.
limitations: Designed for modest condition changes and gives no prediction intervals.
relevance_to_study: Concurrent low-calibrant transfer and calibrant-selection work that complements our calibrant-number analysis but lacks coverage-controlled windows.

authors: Kretschmer F, Harrieder E-M, Witting M, Böcker S
title: Times are changing but order matters: transferable prediction of small-molecule liquid chromatography retention times
verification: Crossref record with abstract, PubMed PMID 42823457 and full text PMC13736644 retrieved this session; public repository README read.
category: Transferable condition-aware retention-order index with anchor mapping
problem: Truly transferable RT prediction that needs no training data from the target system.
data: 171 curated RepoRT RP datasets, six benchmark datasets and a human fecal LC-MS/MS application.
method: D-MPNN GNN with a 13-dimensional condition vector (HSM and Tanaka column parameters, pH) trained by a Siamese margin-ranking loss to predict a retention order index, then mapped to RT by a monotone degree-2 polynomial (LAD outlier removal, then OLS) fitted on anchors.
uncertainty_method: None; only MAE ± SD over folds is reported, and the application used a fixed 0.40 min window equal to the cross-validated anchor MAE.
transfer_setting: No target training data; about 15-30 anchors (standards or confident library hits) on the target RP system.
main_results: Pair-order error rate was 4.89% (versus 5.61% without conditions); 2-step beat DeepGCN-RT and RT-Transformer on 5 of 6 datasets under structure-disjoint splits, and 15 anchors sufficed.
code_available: Yes: github.com/boecker-lab/2-step with model weights and a Docker image, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22093097, and a web app.
limitations: Point predictions only with a heuristic fixed tolerance; HILIC is excluded and anchors are assumed mostly correct.
relevance_to_study: Most direct prior work on our base score and monotone calibrant mapping; our novelty must rest on conformal windows, difficulty normalisation, coverage and decoy evaluation, calibrant-number requirements and HILIC.

authors: Schymanski, E.L.; Jeon, J.; Gulde, R.; Fenner, K.; Ruff, M.; Singer, H.P.; Hollender, J.
title: Identifying Small Molecules via High Resolution Mass Spectrometry: Communicating Confidence
verification: Crossref works record and PubMed PMID 24476540 retrieved in this session; title matches. Neither source has an abstract (2-page viewpoint), so the content fields summarise the standard five-level scheme rather than text read in this session.
category: identification-confidence reporting framework
problem: How to communicate the confidence of HRMS small-molecule identifications consistently across labs.
data: Viewpoint with illustrative environmental HRMS cases; no benchmark dataset.
method: Five-level scale: L1 confirmed structure (reference standard), L2 probable structure (library or diagnostic evidence), L3 tentative candidate(s), L4 unequivocal formula, L5 exact mass of interest.
uncertainty_method: Qualitative evidence levels only; no quantitative treatment of RT deviations or tolerances.
transfer_setting: Not addressed; Level 1 presupposes an authentic standard measured on the lab's own chromatographic system.
main_results: Became the de facto NTS reporting standard. Predicted-RT agreement does not reach Level 1; Kretschmer et al. 2026 call such matches 'almost level 1'.
code_available: Not applicable.
limitations: Qualitative and not automatable; prescribes no RT tolerance and does not quantify ambiguity within the candidate space (critique by Metz et al. 2025).
relevance_to_study: Positions our calibrated RT windows as auditable Level-3 candidate elimination and ranking evidence, filling the RT criterion the scheme leaves unspecified.

authors: Aalizadeh, R.; Nika, M.-C.; Thomaidis, N.S.
title: Development and application of retention time prediction models in the suspect and non-target screening of emerging contaminants
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 30312924 (abstract) retrieved; title matches. Full text not accessible (Elsevier), so the window values are unknown.
category: QSRR RT prediction with error windows for suspect/NTS
problem: Predict tR of emerging contaminants to support suspect and non-target identification in HILIC- and RPLC-HRMS.
data: 682 compounds by HILIC-ESI(+); RPLC sets of 1830 (ESI+) and 308 (ESI-) compounds.
method: Support-vector-machine QSRR models with applicability-domain assessment.
uncertainty_method: Monte Carlo sampling used both for the applicability domain and to derive 'acceptable error windows' for predicted tR (numeric windows not in the abstract).
transfer_setting: System-specific models; the abstract states the error windows were computed for predicted tR 'from various LC conditions'.
main_results: Validated HILIC/RPLC tR models were applied to identify transformation products of emerging contaminants and biocides in wastewater and sludge.
code_available: Not stated in abstract.
limitations: Error windows are fixed per model rather than candidate-adaptive or finite-sample valid, and the models are tied to the training LC conditions.
relevance_to_study: Typical of the heuristic 'acceptable error window' practice that our jackknife+ conformal windows replace.

authors: Ferrando Plo, L.; Kruve, A.
title: Candidate Structure Prioritization in Non-Target Screening with Predicted Collision Cross-Sections and Uncertainty Quantification
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
verification: Crossref record (and ChemRxiv preprint 10.26434/chemrxiv.15006479/v1), PubMed PMID 42789453 and the PMC13663483 full text were read.
category: conformal candidate prioritisation in NTS (CCS)
problem: Replace heuristic relative-CCS thresholds with candidate prioritisation that has a statistical guarantee on retaining true structures.
data: METLIN-CCS (27,377 SMILES; 58,041 ion species) for training and calibration. External in-silico NTS sets from EnvCCS and AllCCS used SIRIUS+CSI:FingerID top-10 candidates (12,464 and 5274 candidates).
method: Normalized Mondrian (by ion type) conformal predictive system wrapped around GraphCCS. The error function is the mean MCES distance to the k nearest training compounds; candidates are kept if P_CCS ≥ α. Includes conformal OOD detection.
uncertainty_method: Conformal predictive distributions normalised by a similarity-based difficulty function, giving recall ≥ 100-α in-domain, plus calibration-conditional correction (δ = 0.05).
transfer_setting: No instrument or system shift. Calibration uses about 1500 library ions per taxonomy from METLIN-CCS; only in-domain candidates (P_OOD ≤ 90%) are evaluated.
main_results: Recall guarantees held in-domain on the external sets. At 90% recall only about 16% of incorrect candidates were removed (at most 8% above random), and only 49% (EnvCCS) and 31% (AllCCS) of ions were in-domain.
code_available: Yes. github.com/kruvelab/CCS-conformal-predictive-distributions (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21487070).
limitations: CCS discriminates isomers poorly; the OOD threshold is heuristic without theory; a large same-distribution calibration set is required; no RT and no cross-laboratory shift.
relevance_to_study: The closest methodological precedent: the same normalised-conformal 'retain ≥ 1-α true structures' logic for NTS, which the authors propose extending to RT. We provide that RT extension under few-calibrant system transfer.

authors: Metz, T.O.; Chang, C.H.; Gautam, V.; Anjum, A.; Tian, S.; Wang, F.; Colby, S.M.; Nunez, J.R.; Blumer, M.R.; Edison, A.S.; Fiehn, O.; Jones, D.P.; Li, S.; Morgan, E.T.; Patti, G.J.; Ross, D.H.; Shapiro, M.R.; Williams, A.J.; Wishart, D.S.
title: Introducing 'Identification Probability' for Automated and Transferable Assessment of Metabolite Identification Confidence in Metabolomics and Related Studies
verification: Crossref record (with abstract), PubMed PMID 39699939 and the PMC11740175 full text were read.
category: identification-probability framework
problem: Quantify the ambiguity of metabolite identifications in an automated, platform-transferable way.
data: In-silico HMDB subsets (22,077 non-lipids; 44,537 lipids) with predicted m/z, CCS (CCSbase), RT (Retip; HILIC or RP) and MS/MS (CFM-ID 4.0).
method: Identification probability IP = 1/N, where N is the number of library compounds matching within user-set tolerances across all measured dimensions.
uncertainty_method: User-defined hard tolerances: RT ±0.1 or ±0.5 min; m/z ±0.1-5 ppm; CCS ±0.1-3%; MS/MS cosine ≥ 750-950.
transfer_setting: Assumes library properties are valid on the user's platform; no explicit RT transfer.
main_results: RT alone never gave unique matches at either tolerance. Adding RT to m/z, CCS and MS/MS raised the fraction of unambiguous matches, more so at ±0.1 min.
code_available: Not stated (perspective with SI).
limitations: Hard tolerances ignore prediction uncertainty and heteroscedasticity; IP depends on library completeness; demonstration is purely in silico.
relevance_to_study: The RT tolerance directly sets the candidate count N, so our calibrated, candidate-specific windows give a principled tolerance for IP-style counting.

authors: Ngan, H.-L.; Turkina, V.; van Herwerden, D.; Yan, H.; Cai, Z.; Samanipour, S.
title: Machine Learning for Enhanced Identification Probability in RPLC/HRMS Nontargeted Workflows
verification: Crossref record, PubMed PMID 40791078 and the PMC12392258 full text were read.
category: learned true-positive probability using predicted RTI
problem: Raise identification probability of spectral-library matches in RPLC/HRMS NTA when retention information is missing.
data: 4713 calibrants on three harmonised RTI scales (fingerprint-to-RTI model); 485,577 MS/MS spectra (CNL-to-RTI model); 1,686,319 TP and semisynthetic TN matches; pesticide spikes in blanks and black-tea matrices.
method: Random-forest fingerprint-to-RTI and CNL-to-RTI regressors. A KNN classifier on the RTI discrepancy plus mass and spectral-match features gives P(TP); IP comes from averaged P(TP).
uncertainty_method: No intervals. The RTI discrepancy is a learned feature, with a leverage-based applicability domain and a P(TP) cut-off of 0.5.
transfer_setting: Calibrant-free: RTIs are inferred from the candidate structure and from the query spectrum, so no measured RT or system calibration is used.
main_results: Weighted F1 0.65 and MCC 0.30 in blanks. At P(TP) ≥ 0.5 the TP rate was 98.8% at an FP rate of 23.4%. IPs rose 46.7-54.5% over library matching alone.
code_available: Yes. GitHub TommyNHL/exposomeIDProba and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16402775.
limitations: Ignores the measured RT, so it cannot separate spectrally similar isomers by elution; large RTI errors (MAE 111 RTI units, MRE 27.5% on untrained calibrants) limit specificity.
relevance_to_study: An alternative soft-scoring route that is probabilistic but uncalibrated. Contrasts with our measured-RT conformal filter and could consume our window-based evidence.

authors: Bach, E.; Rogers, S.; Williamson, J.; Rousu, J.
title: Probabilistic framework for integration of mass spectrum and retention time information in small molecule identification
verification: Crossref record (with abstract), PubMed PMID 33244585 and the PMC8289373 full text were read.
category: retention-order-aware joint candidate scoring
problem: Combine MS-based candidate scores with retention information from all features of an LC-MS run to rank structures.
data: CASMI 2016 (208 MS2-RT tuples) and EA/MassBank (473 tuples). RankSVM trained on seven public RT datasets (four columns; H2O to MeOH with 0.1% formic acid).
method: Pairwise Markov random field: MS2 (IOKR) or MS1 node potentials, RankSVM retention-order edge potentials, max-marginals from random spanning-tree ensembles.
uncertainty_method: Platt-calibrated sigmoid on RankSVM margins; no RT intervals.
transfer_setting: Uses retention order, so absolute RT shifts are tolerated; the RankSVM was trained on RTs from other systems.
main_results: Significant top-k gains over MS2-only scoring and over the RT integrations of MetFrag 2.2 and the chain-graph method, including when only some features have MS2.
code_available: Yes. github.com/aalto-ics-kepaco/msms_rt_score_integration.
limitations: Order changes across different mobile phases or columns are not modelled; no candidate filtering or guarantee of retaining the true structure.
relevance_to_study: Precedent for cross-system retention-order learning in identification. Our pairwise-ranking base score builds on it but outputs calibrated per-candidate RT windows.

authors: Bach, E.; Schymanski, E.L.; Rousu, J.
title: Joint structural annotation of small molecules using liquid chromatography retention order and tandem mass spectrometry data
verification: Crossref record (with abstract) and bioRxiv API abstract (preprint 10.1101/2022.02.11.480137) retrieved; not indexed in PubMed; publisher full text not accessible.
category: structured prediction of annotations using retention order
problem: Jointly annotate all MS features of an LC-MS2 run using observed retention orders and MS2 scorer outputs.
data: All public reversed-phase LC-MS2 data in MassBank: 4,327 molecules from 18 LC conditions and 16 contributors.
method: LC-MS2Struct: a structured SVM combining CFM-ID, MetFrag and SIRIUS scores with observed retention orders, using stereochemistry-aware fingerprints.
uncertainty_method: None (max-margin scoring, no intervals).
transfer_setting: Uses retention orders within each LC condition; no absolute RT transfer.
main_results: Significantly higher annotation accuracy than earlier methods; improved the accuracy of state-of-the-art MS2 scorers by up to 106%.
code_available: Yes. Repositories aalto-ics-kepaco/msms_rt_ssvm and aalto-ics-kepaco/lcms2struct_exp were identified by web search but not opened.
limitations: Needs many co-measured features in a run; gives no per-candidate RT window or filtering guarantee; stereoisomers remain hard.
relevance_to_study: State of the art for soft retention-order integration, and a reference point for what calibrated absolute-RT windows add for single features and isomeric decoys.

authors: Ruttkies, C.; Schymanski, E.L.; Wolf, S.; Hollender, J.; Neumann, S.
title: MetFrag relaunched: incorporating strategies beyond in silico fragmentation
verification: Crossref record, PubMed PMID 26834843 and the PMC4732001 full text were read.
category: in-silico candidate ranking with an RT score
problem: Rank database candidates for HR-MS/MS spectra by combining in-silico fragmentation with metadata, including RT.
data: 473 merged HR-MS/MS spectra (Eawag/MassBank), plus three validation sets totalling 824 spectra.
method: Weighted sum of fragmenter, RT, reference and suspect scores. The RT score comes from a linear logP-RT fit on user standards (at least ten recommended) and a Gaussian density of the logP deviation with σ = 1.5.
uncertainty_method: Fixed Gaussian width σ = 1.5 logP units, described as 'chosen arbitrarily'; no calibration.
transfer_setting: In-situ calibration: standards measured on the user's own system fit the logP-RT model.
main_results: Top-1 ranks rose from 30 (MS/MS only, PubChem) to 336 (PubChem) and 420 (ChemSpider) when reference and RT information were added.
code_available: Yes. MetFrag CLI (c-ruttkies.github.io/MetFrag).
limitations: logP is a weak RT proxy for ionisable or polar compounds; the score width is arbitrary; the RT contribution is confounded with reference scores in the headline results.
relevance_to_study: The canonical NTS soft-scoring baseline with an ad hoc RT width. Our conformal scale can replace σ with a calibrated, candidate-adaptive width.

authors: Hupatz, H.; Rahu, I.; Wang, W.-C.; Peets, P.; Palm, E.H.; Kruve, A.
title: Critical review on in silico methods for structural annotation of chemicals detected with LC/HRMS non-targeted screening
verification: Crossref record (with abstract), PubMed PMID 39138659 and the PMC11700063 full text were read.
category: critical review and case study of NTS candidate prioritisation
problem: Review in-silico candidate retrieval and prioritisation (RT, CCS, ionisation) for LC/HRMS NTS and test them on real features.
data: Wastewater case study: 10 spiked chemicals and 10 unknown features; 515 unique candidates from MassBank, MetFrag, SIRIUS+CSI:FingerID and Spec2Mol.
method: Prioritisation with RTI-model RT using a ±2 standardized-residual cut-off and CCSbase CCS within 3%.
uncertainty_method: Fixed residual-based cut-offs; no coverage control.
transfer_setting: NORMAN RTI calibration to the lab's system.
main_results: The RT filter kept 255 of 515 candidates but deprioritised the correct structure for 2 of 10 spiked chemicals. Combining RT and CCS removed every candidate for 1 spiked and 2 unknown features.
code_available: Yes. github.com/kruvelab/NTS_LC_HRMS, plus an SI CSV of all candidates and prioritisation outcomes.
limitations: Only 20 features; RTI model applicability gaps (e.g. a boron-containing candidate could not be predicted); the authors attribute poor efficiency to high prediction uncertainty.
relevance_to_study: Documents both low efficiency and losses of true structures with heuristic RT cut-offs, and calls for uncertainty-aware evaluation metrics, which is our core motivation.

authors: McEachran, A.D.; Mansouri, K.; Newton, S.R.; Beverly, B.E.J.; Sobus, J.R.; Williams, A.J.
title: A comparison of three liquid chromatography (LC) retention time prediction models
verification: Crossref record, PubMed PMID 29501166 and the PMC6066181 full text were read.
category: RT-window filtering with measured true-positive loss
problem: Compare RT prediction models and RT screening windows for reducing candidate lists in non-targeted analysis.
data: 97 chemicals (78 training, 19 test) on an Eclipse Plus C8 45-min gradient; top-10 CompTox Dashboard candidates per test formula.
method: EPI Suite logP linear model vs ACD/ChromGenius vs OPERA-RT QSRR; candidates screened with ±2, ±3 and ±5 min windows.
uncertainty_method: Fixed absolute windows or fractions of run time (±5-20%); no calibration.
transfer_setting: Single in-house system; models trained on that system.
main_results: ±5 min removed about 20% of candidates while keeping 18/19 (ACD) and 17/19 (OPERA-RT) true chemicals. At ±3 min OPERA-RT removed 60% vs 40% but kept only 42% vs 83% of true chemicals. Zero-loss windows would have needed 5.06 and 6.5 min.
code_available: Not stated; training and test data and candidate tables in the supplementary material.
limitations: Very small training and test sets; one system; candidate lists pre-filtered to the top 10 by data-source count.
relevance_to_study: Quantifies the trade-off between removing false candidates and losing true positives with fixed windows, which motivates coverage-controlled windows and our recall-vs-elimination evaluation.

authors: Samaraweera, M.A.; Hall, L.M.; Hill, D.W.; Grant, D.F.
title: Evaluation of an Artificial Neural Network Retention Index Model for Chemical Structure Identification in Nontargeted Metabolomics
verification: Crossref DOI from the PubMed record (PMID 30350614) and the PMC8378237 full text were read; title matches.
category: RI filtering with similarity-adaptive windows and measured false-negative rate
problem: Remove false-positive candidates before in-silico MS/MS ranking using a predicted retention index.
data: 91 endogenous metabolites not in the RI training set; PubChem and HMDB candidate sets retrieved at ±15 ppm.
method: ANN retention-index model (C3-C14 n-amide scale); candidates outside the window removed before CFM-ID, CSI:FingerID, Mass Frontier or MetFrag ranking.
uncertainty_method: Windows of ±2SE (52.4 RIU) for candidates structurally similar to the training data (bit-key match) and ±3SE (78.6 RIU) otherwise, intended to give 95% sensitivity.
transfer_setting: Same-lab RI system anchored by n-amide homologues.
main_results: 12 of 91 true structures were eliminated (87% sensitivity, against 4-5 expected losses). The filter removed 58% of PubChem false candidates and roughly halved average ranks for three fragmenters. Widening by 0.5 SE gave 90% sensitivity at 53% specificity.
code_available: Not stated.
limitations: Single system, small test set, heuristic similarity bins; coverage particularly poor in the mid-RI range.
relevance_to_study: Direct evidence that nominal ±2SE windows under-cover and that novelty-aware widening helps. This is the gap our meta-learned difficulty normalisation with conformal calibration targets.

authors: Rakhshaninejad, M.; De Waele, G.; Jürgens, M.; Waegeman, W.
title: Reliable Molecular Retrieval from Mass Spectra Using Conformal Prediction
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
verification: Crossref record and PubMed PMID 42113637 (abstract) retrieved; title matches. Full text not accessed.
category: conformal prediction sets for MS/MS candidate retrieval
problem: Turn candidate rankings from MS/MS retrieval into spectrum-specific sets that contain the true molecule with a user-specified probability.
data: MassSpecGym benchmark under in-distribution, partially shifted and fully out-of-distribution scenarios.
method: Marginal and conditional (group-wise) conformal prediction on fingerprint-similarity candidate rankings.
uncertainty_method: Split conformal prediction, with conditional variants (e.g. confidence-based grouping) for subgroup reliability.
transfer_setting: Explicit evaluation under distribution shift between calibration and test spectra.
main_results: Target coverage with small sets when calibration matches test data; sets grow under shift; conditional conformal improves subgroup reliability, best with confidence-based grouping.
code_available: Not stated in abstract.
limitations: MS/MS only (no RT); requires representative calibration spectra; efficiency degrades under shift.
relevance_to_study: Shows conformal candidate sets entering small-molecule MS identification and the value of difficulty-conditional calibration under shift. Complementary to, and combinable with, our RT-window layer.
